text:
Erin (AE): Heads up — Acero wants an updated order form that includes a 'quantified usage credit' line for the POC. They want 200k tokens/mo credit for 3 months instead of an up-front discount. Also they asked if we can reduce SLA uptime from 99.9% to 99.5 for the POC window. Finance flagged that we need PO before e-sign and KMS key handoff is required. Thoughts?
Sam (Solutions Eng): For the POC we can scope the token credit as a billing credit applied at invoice, simple to do. Pricing impact is minimal. Regarding SLA, 99.5% for a 3-month POC is OK but ops needs to add fallback routing.
Priya (Sales Ops): @Erin FYI finance will only accept net-30 PO if legal ok with the MSA/DPA redlines. Can we get a PO number before we send DocuSign? If customer refuses, we'll need an exception and an exec signoff.
Marta (Legal): Share the redlines they proposed. Quick note: we rarely change SLA figures in the MSA — prefer an addendum for the POC with explicit term: "POC Term: 3 months, SLA 99.5%" and indemnity stays the same. Also KMS key custody note: we need KMS integration appendix and key rotation responsibilities documented.
Erin (AE): Copy of customer redlines pasted below. They've added: 1) quantified usage credit table 2) lower SLA for POC 3) "customer-managed KMS" clause that implies we hold zero key access.
Erin (AE): ````
Order Form snippet:
- POC Credits: 200,000 tokens per month, applied as invoice credit for months 1-3
- SLA: 99.5% uptime during POC term
- KMS: Customer-managed; provider shall not have access to plaintext keys
````
Sam (Solutions Eng): :eyes: For customer-managed KMS we can support BYOK but must document that features like KV-cache snapshotting require encrypted-in-transit/decrypt on instance; we can offer an optional managed-encrypt path with HSM if they need ops assistance.
Priya (Sales Ops): We need a clean signature flow. Proposal: customer sends PO -> we countersign order form via DocuSign -> post-sign we begin KMS handoff. If they insist on e-sign before PO, we should attach a billing contingency clause.
Marta (Legal): Draft language for contingency: "Commencement of services is contingent upon receipt of an authorized purchase order or equivalent billing instrument. In the absence of such instrument within 30 days of countersignature, Provider may suspend billing and/or services." That buys us protection.
Erin (AE): Can you drop that into the order form? Also they asked if credits can apply to overage at a reduced rate — they'd like overflow tokens billed at 50% list rate until credits exhausted.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Overflow billing at 50% list is fine for POC, but need explicit definition of "tokens" and measurement window. Suggest add: "Token units measured on a per-UTC-month basis using Provider billing meter."
Priya (Sales Ops): Operational steps for us: 1) Obtain PO 2) Legal to approve addendum 3) Send DocuSign with addendum + contingency clause 4) Finance to apply credit line on invoice. Assigning tasks: @Erin to collect PO, @Marta to provide draft addendum, @Priya to prepare billing template.
Marta (Legal): Drafted addendum attached (link): https://redwood-internal.share/addenda/acero-poc-addendum-draft. Key points included: limited SLA, POC termination rights, KMS appendix referencing customer responsibility, billing credit mechanics, and a clause for overage rate. Please review and call out any blockers.
Erin (AE): I'll ping the customer for PO. Also they want signature roles: Customer legal sig + engineering sig (two signers). Can DocuSign handle two signers in parallel?
Priya (Sales Ops): Yes, DocuSign supports parallel signing. We'll set routing: customer legal -> customer eng -> provider AE -> provider finance (counterparty). Finance prefers to be in the loop but not mandatory signer.
contract-bot: Note: Our DocuSign template "orderform-v3" supports addenda attachments and parallel signer routing. Template ID: tmpl-ord-v3. Use field tags: sign1_legal, sign2_eng, sign3_provider.
Marta (Legal): One more — limit liability: for POC only cap damages to amount actually paid under the POC. Addendum should say that.
Erin (AE): Great. I'll try to get PO today. If not, we'll request exec exception. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Priya (Sales Ops): I'll stand by to spin up DocuSign envelope once @Marta drops final text.
Sam (Solutions Eng): If you want, I can create a short tech note describing the KMS handoff steps for customer engineering. Might smooth approvals.
Erin (AE): Please do, Sam. Send it into the thread when ready.
Marta (Legal): Sending final addendum in 2 hrs.
Erin (AE): Update: customer confirmed PO will be sent EOD; they requested the DocuSign envelope to be ready so they can sign immediately when PO is in.
Priya (Sales Ops): I'll prepare envelope with placeholder PO field and parallel routing. @Erin paste PO when received.
contract-bot: Action logged: envelope prepped with template tmpl-ord-v3; waiting for PO value to autofill. Reference ID: env-48219.
Erin (AE): Closing loop — PO number 45001987 received and pasted into envelope. Moving to signatures.
Marta (Legal): Confirming final redlines accepted — proceeding to countersign after customer completes signatures.
Priya (Sales Ops): :white_check_mark: Done, envelope completed.
Erin (AE): Signed and countersigned. KMS handoff scheduled for next Tue. Thanks team! :thumbsup:
